title: fix(service-automation)!: a disabled package's flow it ships alone is neither fired nor served bare, and the served holder of a shared name keeps its slot key (ADR-0150 D3)
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"zhuangjianguo"} -->
_Requested by **Steedos** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_018ETKaNwMZCNRYD7D8Q9Ubb?thread=cmsg_018ETKaNwMZCNRYD7D8Q9UbbCpddLFmKzR39wJWZpkRMCi)_
Fixes #33893
Fixes #33905

Clause-②: no (narrowing)
Metadata-protocol: none
Skills-docs: none — no published skill teaches what a trigger or the bare automation entries do for a flow whose package is disabled, or how the engine keys a flow two packages ship (`skills/objectstack-automation` names a disabled package only for a packaged flow's queue approver)

> **BREAKING** (#33905) for a deployment where a package that alone ships a flow name is disabled while the engine still holds that flow (the re-sync that follows a disable failed or did not run): the flow no longer runs on its trigger, and the engine's bare entries (`execute`, `getFlow`, `toggleFlow`) answer as for a flow they do not hold, so the bare HTTP doors answer `404`, the answer the namespaced address already gave. Remedy: enable the package. No key, row or binding moves, so nothing is migrated (ADR-0087: `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`). #33893 alone is `Clause-②: no`: it restores a served holder's trigger.

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么:两张卡(#33905 一个提交,#33893 三个提交,另有两个 changeset 文字提交)。#33905:一个流程名只有一个包持有、该包被停用而引擎仍持有其槽位时,触发器不再运行它(每个槽位只记一行 info),引擎裸入口 execute/getFlow/toggleFlow 按"没有这个流程"回答(HTTP 裸门因此答 404,与命名空间地址一致);重新启用即恢复,无需重新挂载。#33893:两个包持有同名流程、其中一个被停用时,仍在服务的那个包的槽位保持 `PACKAGE/NAME` 键、保持挂载并正常触发(开机时不再被误判为 M1 拒绝并打出误导警告;运行中撤回停用包的槽位时不再改键、不再停掉绑定);停用的包重新启用时,重同步无论先注册哪个包,两个槽位都挂上触发器、不再误报"流程体被拒绝";停用的包随后被卸载时,在服务的槽位在下一次注册、触发或被按名访问时折回裸名,删除、版本历史、回滚、裸 inbound hook、凭据照常可用,重同步失败也不会让它不可达。
- 为什么改:座席裁决 6884403301 修正 7「停用可逆,不移动任何键」;#33905 的座席裁决 B(停用的包不持有任何名字,ADR-0150 D3)。
- 风险与回滚:#33905 是破坏性收窄(标题带 `!`),只影响"包已停用但重同步没撤掉槽位"的流程;停用期间的触发事件直接丢弃、启用后不补跑;克隆门以该流程名为新名时由 409 变为放行,与重同步撤回该流程后克隆门本来的答复一致(席位已裁定:不是放宽,`Clause-②: no (narrowing)` 不变)。#33893 只改槽位键的归档规则,M1(另一个在服务的包的流程体真被拒绝)行为不变。槽位键、运行键、绑定、`flowDispatchHolder`、凭据、版本历史都按全部持有者判断,不迁移。已暂停运行的恢复不在本 PR 决定。回滚即还原本 PR。
- 先看:`packages/services/service-automation/src/flow-slots.ts` 的 `add`/`remove`/`isShared`(`coHeldByDisabled`);`settle`(卸载后折回裸名);`engine.ts` 的 `placeFlowSlot`(折回与回归时补挂在位槽位)、`activateFlowTrigger` 的 M1 判断(限定键槽位只在记录到拒绝时才拒挂)、`settleFlowName` 的调用点、`loneSharedFlowKey`(M1 改为只看在服务的持有者)、`triggerRun` 的停用判断、`resolveFlowKey`/`servedBareFlowKey` 新增的 `isDisabledSoleHolder`。
- 两分钟验证:`pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-automation exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/flow-slots-per-package.test.ts`,预期 91 个全部通过,其中 `[#33905]` 与 `[#33893]` 两个 describe 共 27 个新用例。
- 需要你做的:无,席位落地。

## What changes

**#33905 (commit 1): a flow whose only holder's package is disabled.** PR #33546 withdraws a disabled package's flows on the normal path (the disable's re-sync); this closes the case where the engine still holds the slot. One predicate, `isDisabledHolderSlot` (PR #33890's, asked of the one resolver with the slot's package as the caller: the registry holds that package's flow of the name AND the package is disabled), now judges the slot of a name one package holds too:

- `triggerRun`: the fire-time gate covers a slot of an unshared name. The skip is said once per slot at `info`, said again after the slot dispatched once more; a re-enable dispatches with no re-arm. This flips PR #33890's single-holder CONTROL ("as on `main` today").
- `resolveFlowKey` (the run's read, not the `durable` one) and `servedBareFlowKey`: a disabled sole holder is `absent`, so `execute` (any caller, a `subflow` / `map` node's call included), `getFlow` and `toggleFlow` answer as for a flow this engine does not hold.

What moves, for such a flow while its package is disabled (FROM → TO):

| Entry | FROM | TO |
|---|---|---|
| its trigger binding (record-change, schedule, time-relative, an api hook's queued post) | runs the flow | nothing runs, no run-history row; said once at `info` |
| `execute(name, …)`, any caller, subflow / map calls included | runs the flow | `{ success: false, error: "Flow 'NAME' not found" }` |
| `getFlow(name)` | the flow | `null` |
| bare HTTP doors that probe `getFlow` (`GET /automation/NAME`, `POST /automation/NAME/trigger`, `POST /automation/trigger/NAME`, `POST /automation/NAME/toggle`, `POST /automation/NAME/clone`, `GET /automation/NAME/runs`) | served | `404`, as the namespaced address `/automation/NAMESPACE/NAME…` answers |
| `toggleFlow(name, …)` | switches the flow | rejects `Flow 'NAME' not found` |
| `POST /automation/SOURCE/clone` with this flow's name as the new name (taken-name probe `getFlow(NEW)`) | `409` name taken | the probe admits the copy. On the engine (measured), a registration with no package lands the copy's body in the disabled package's slot, and once the package is re-enabled, its trigger runs the copy's body until the next re-sync. This is the answer the door already gives once the disable's re-sync has withdrawn the flow, so the door admits nothing the normal path refuses. The seat ruled it no widening (contract record 6900695384), and `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` stands |
| a definition write (`POST /automation`, `PUT /automation/NAME`) or clone that the engine accepts and that is then refused (unknown `notify` channel, refused landing or save) | puts back the definition the engine held | nothing to put back: `unregisterFlow(NAME)` drops the package's registration |
| `PUT /automation/NAME` with a body that leaves out a stored credential (`keepStoredFlowCredentials`) | keeps the credential the engine held | carries nothing forward |
| `DELETE /automation/NAME` | answers a deletion | still removes the engine's registration (`bareFlowKey`, read over every holder); answers `404` unless a stored row was removed |

The four write-door rows were read from `packages/runtime/src/domains/automation.ts` at this head. Each applies only where the door's earlier guards (`packagedBaseRefusal`, `tenantAuthoredWriteRefusal`, the clone's first-write pin) admit the request, and the full door is not measured. The engine half of the clone row was measured: probe `null`, copy filed in the package's slot, its body run on re-enable. These doors ask `getFlow` a durable question, so they belong on a durable read. That is a runtime change outside this claim, carded as #34145.

Remedy: enable the package. Not moved (condition 2): the slot key, run keys, the trigger binding, `flowDispatchHolder`, credentials and the version history stay judged over every holder. **Parked-run resume is NOT decided here.** A package-less flow (the environment's own, or one registered straight into the engine) and an engine with no resolver are CONTROLs.

**#33893 (commits `9d712d1d`, `7c193056`, `ea75f64d`): the served holder of a name a disabled package co-holds.** `FlowSlotTable` takes a second predicate, `coHeldByDisabled(name)`: the registry holds the name under two or more packages (every holder, R4-G's `heldByMany`) and at most one of them is served.

- `add`: the first package slot of such a name is filed under `PACKAGE/NAME`, not the bare name (the boot pull with one holder disabled).
- `remove`: a co-holder's removal moves no key while the predicate holds (the disable's re-sync withdrawing the disabled holder's slot), so the served slot keeps its key and its binding.
- The co-holder's return (the enable's re-sync registers every contender, in precedence's order):
  - `activateFlowTrigger`: a lone slot filed under its qualified key takes the M1 decline only once another package's body of the name is recorded as refused (`flowRefusals`). So when the served holder registers first, it is armed, with no "whose body was refused" warning; a co-holder the re-sync has not reached yet is no refusal.
  - `placeFlowSlot`: when the co-holder's slot is added beside an incumbent already under its qualified key, no key moves, so the incumbent's re-arm (the one a move would have done) is done there.
  - `recordFlowRefusal`: a refusal recorded after such a slot was armed still declines it, and now says the warning.
- `settle`, the fold back: once the registry no longer holds the name twice (the disabled holder uninstalled), the lone slot kept under `PACKAGE/NAME` folds back to the bare name through `moveFlowRecords`, the record move a withdrawal uses. It is asked (`settleFlowName`) the first time the engine:
  - places the slot again (`placeFlowSlot`);
  - fires it (`triggerRun`, and that event runs where the slot lands);
  - reads the name (`resolveFlowKey`, `bareFlowKey`, `servedBareFlowKey`, `inboundHookSlot`).

  So a failed re-sync leaves no unreachable flow. `isShared` is `main`'s again (slot count, or the registry holding the name twice), so a name one package holds is never read as shared. Removal, version history, rollback, withdraw, the bare inbound hook and the credential source serve it.
- `loneSharedFlowKey` (the M1 decline, its warning, `recordFlowRefusal`, `getFlowRegistration`): M1 now needs two SERVED holders, so the decline and the "whose body was refused" warning stay for a body another served package really had refused, and a disabled co-holder is no M1.

A holder that leaves the registry (uninstall) before its slot is withdrawn folds the name back to its bare key at the withdrawal, as before (CONTROL).

## Tests

`packages/services/service-automation/src/flow-slots-per-package.test.ts` (the shared harness file, per the AGENTS.md rule that a new pin for a component with a shared harness goes into that file as a top-level `describe`), over the real `SchemaRegistry`, the real `flowNameResolver` and a recording trigger:

- `[#33748]` describe: its single-holder CONTROL is flipped to `[#33905] a name one package holds, disabled at runtime with its slot left armed: not dispatched, said once; re-enabled, it dispatches with no re-arm`.
- `[#33905] the bare entries of a flow whose only holder's package is disabled` (4): `execute` / `getFlow` / `toggleFlow` equal the answers for a name the engine does not hold, durable reads unmoved, re-enable serves again; a subflow call reaches no flow; CONTROLs: a package-less flow, no resolver.
- `[#33893] the served holder of a name a disabled package co-holds keeps its qualified key, armed` (23):
  - the `FlowSlotTable` unit, `settle` included;
  - in both registry orders and for each holder disabled, a boot disable (registry holds both, one disabled before the pull) and a runtime disable followed by the re-sync's `withdrawFlowSlot`;
  - for the runtime disable → withdraw order and for the boot-disable order, the disabled holder then uninstalled and the uninstall's re-sync re-registering the served holder: key `t`, trigger armed under `t` and dispatching, `inboundHookSlot('t')` `undefined` (served, not refused), `getFlowVersionHistory('t')` the slot's two versions, `execute`, and `unregisterFlow('t')` removing it;
  - the co-holder's return, for the boot disable and the runtime disable, each holder disabled, with the re-sync registering the served holder first and the returning one first (8): both slots armed and dispatched, no refused-body warning;
  - CONTROL: the returning holder's body really is refused. The served one is declined behind the warning, said once; when the returning holder is registered after all, both are armed;
  - the stretch between the uninstall and any re-registration (a failed re-sync), first touched by the trigger (the event runs the flow, then the slot is under `t` with its binding) and first touched by a bare entry (`inboundHookSlot`, `getFlow`, version history, `execute` serve it);
  - CONTROL: an uninstall before the withdraw folds the key back.

`packages/runtime/src/domains/automation-addressed-route.test.ts`, new describe `[#33905] … the bare door answers as its namespaced address (404)` over a real `SchemaRegistry` and the real dispatcher: for a disabled sole holder each bare door (`GET`, `trigger`, legacy trigger, `toggle`, `runs`) answers `404` with the code its address answers, nothing runs or switches; the clone door with the flow as its source answers `404` as its address does, and nothing is registered; CONTROL: enabled, both serve. The service double answers what the engine now answers (the engine half is pinned above). No runtime source changed, so this pin is not ablated; its moving half is ablated as A3 below.

## Acceptance notes

- **The boot pull's first holder of a name two SERVED packages ship is declined behind the refused-body warning until the second registers (finding, not changed).** Measured on the engine with this PR's sources (a local commit before the merge), both packages enabled and the registry holding both before the pull: the refused-body warning was said once (`refusedBodyWarnings=1`) and the first slot was re-armed only by the second holder's key move. No body was refused. It predates this PR (unchanged here: M1 still reads every served holder, and telling "refused" from "not yet registered" needs the refusal record, which the ObjectQL-registry pull does not write). Raised in the report for its own card.
- **`execute` is gated for every caller**, as the shared-name rule already is (`servedCaller`, amendment 4), so a `subflow` / `map` call of such a flow now gets no flow; listed in the FROM → TO table.
- **Doors that read `getFlow` for a durable question** (the clone door's name-taken probe, the definition writes' rollback copy and carried-forward credentials, the DELETE door's existence probe, the flow-start admission's definition read) see `null` for such a flow. The rows above name what moves. Moving them onto a durable read is a runtime change outside this claim, carded as #34145 (the boot pull's bare-key first-holder decline is #34051).
- **Engine readers that are not entries** (the subflow guards' call key, the activation-row key, `packagedFlowOwner`) do not fold the slot themselves. Between an uninstall and the first fold they read the bare name, and the first registration, fire or bare read folds it.
- **`getFlowRuntimeStates` / `listFlows`** still report a disabled sole holder's flow as bound and listed while its trigger is gated (review#2 N2, outside condition 1; unchanged).
- **Deviation from the order's suggested route:** the pins are top-level `describe`s in the shared harness files rather than new per-card files (AGENTS.md, ruling record 6583487846).
